\section{Turing Machine --- Build --- Loop}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.Loop
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\subsection*{Turing Machine --- Build --- Loop: Introduction}

This module provides the bounded-loop control centerpiece of the machine-construction
library for multi-tape Turing machines over the Boolean alphabet. Its public results are
the loop summation lemma, the configuration-level, decision, and result-bearing loop
combinators (a fuel machine lays down a binary round counter, and a body machine is
called once per round between visits to an anchor state), the emitting loop combinator
whose rounds append output chunks, and the install- and emit-mode clean-call bridges
that package any time-bounded function witness as a callable module with clean entry and
exit seams. The supporting material constructs and verifies the concrete loop
controllers phase by phase: fuel capture and counter setup, the stop-wrapped body calls,
the fixed-width counter countdown, payload replay, tracked-bank evaluation, native
interval cleanup, and result finalization.

\subsection*{Turing Machine --- Build --- Loop: Results}

\begin{definition}[Standard word assignment for seam configurations]
\lean{Turing.stateWord}
\label{Turing.stateWord}
\leanok
For a tape count $k$ and a Boolean word $s$, the assignment of one word per work tape
that places $s$ on tape $0$ and the empty word on every other tape. It is the standard
tape content of a loop body's round-boundary (seam) configurations: round state on tape
zero, all scratch blank.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Bounded computation over successive rounds]
\lean{Turing.loop_run}
\label{Turing.loop_run}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add}
\difficulty{5}
Let $M$ be a multi-tape Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $x$ be a finite
Boolean input, and let $c_j$ be a configuration on that input for each natural number
$j$. Let $a$ be a Boolean-valued predicate on the natural numbers, and let $B,N$ be
natural numbers. Suppose that $c_j$ has empty output for every $j\le N$, that from $c_N$
the machine halts within $B$ steps with output the single bit $0$, and that for each
$j<N$, if $a(j)$ is true then from $c_j$ the machine halts within $B$ steps with output
the single bit $1$, while if $a(j)$ is false then within $B$ steps it reaches exactly
$c_{j+1}$. Then from $c_0$ the machine halts within $(N+1)B$ steps, with output the
single bit indicating whether $a(j)$ is true for at least one $j<N$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Liveness propagates to earlier times]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.loop_live_prefix}
\label{Turing.FinTM.loop_live_prefix}
\leanok

\difficulty{3}

of $M$. If after $t$ steps from $c$ the machine has not halted, then for every $u \le t$

\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Invariant along an iterated orbit]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.loop_orbit_inv}
\label{Turing.FinTM.loop_orbit_inv}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
Let $I$ be a predicate on pairs of Boolean words, let $F$ map a Boolean word and a
Boolean word to a Boolean word, and let $s_0$ assign a Boolean word to each Boolean
word. Suppose $I(x,s_0(x))$ holds for every Boolean word $x$, and whenever $I(x,s)$
holds, so does $I(x,F(x,s))$. Then for every Boolean word $x$ and every natural number
$i$, the predicate $I$ holds of $x$ and the result of iterating $s\mapsto F(x,s)$
exactly $i$ times starting at $s_0(x)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Binary output length and running time]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.loop_fuel_width}
\label{Turing.FinTM.loop_fuel_width}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesFunInTime, Turing.MultiTapeTM.output_length_le}
\difficulty{2}
Let $F$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, and let
$R,T:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. Suppose that on every input word $y$, the machine halts
within $T(|y|)$ steps with output the binary digit word of $R(|y|)$. Then, for every
Boolean word $x$, the length of the binary digit word of $R(|x|)$ is at most $T(|x|)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Bounded rewind of the input head]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.loop_rewind_bounded}
\label{Turing.FinTM.loop_rewind_bounded}
\leanok

\difficulty{5}
Let $M$ be a multi-tape Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $s$ and $r$ be
states, and let $d$ be an optional state. Suppose that every transition from $s$,
regardless of the scanned symbols, moves the input head one position left and enters
$r$; every transition from $r$ moves the head one position left and remains in $r$ when

\le p+2$, where $p$ is the input-head position of $c$, at which the machine is in state
$d$ with input-head position $1$, and every other component of $c$ is unchanged.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Fixed-width little-endian decrement]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.loopDebit}
\label{Turing.FinTM.loopDebit}
\leanok
For a Boolean word read as a little-endian binary counter, the pair of the decremented
word and a success flag: the lowest $\mathrm{true}$ cell is cleared and all lower cells
are set to $\mathrm{true}$, returning success; if no cell is $\mathrm{true}$
(underflow), every existing cell is set to $\mathrm{true}$ and the flag is
$\mathrm{false}$. The word length never changes and the empty word reports underflow.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Length of the borrow scan]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.loopBorrowPos}
\label{Turing.FinTM.loopBorrowPos}
\leanok
For a Boolean word read as a little-endian counter, the number of low $\mathrm{false}$
cells traversed by a borrow; it equals the length of the maximal $\mathrm{false}$ prefix
of the word.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Bound on the Borrow Scan]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.loopBorrowPos_le}
\label{Turing.FinTM.loopBorrowPos_le}
\leanok

\difficulty{3}

\end{lemma}

\lean{Turing.FinTM.loopDebit_length}

\begin{definition}[One-tape counter decrement machine]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.loopDebitTM}
\label{Turing.FinTM.loopDebitTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.controlAction}
A bundled finite machine over the Boolean alphabet with one work tape that performs a
fixed-width little-endian decrement followed by a rewind to cell zero. Its live control
states are a borrow state, rewind states remembering the success flag, and silent
waiting return states indexed by that flag; no transition emits physical output.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Configuration of the decrement machine]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.loopDebitCfg}
\label{Turing.FinTM.loopDebitCfg}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.FinTM.loopDebitTM}
For an input word $x$, an input-head position $p$, a control state $q$, a work head
position $z$, and a counter word $u$, the configuration of the one-tape counter
decrement machine whose single work tape is the buffer tape of $u$, with head at $z$,
control $q$, input head at $p$, and empty output.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[One borrow transition of the decrement machine]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.loopBorrow_step}
\label{Turing.FinTM.loopBorrow_step}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.FinTM.loopBuffer_read, Turing.FinTM.loopBuffer_write, Turing.FinTM.loopDebitCfg, Turing.FinTM.loopDebitTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.moveInputPos_zero}
\difficulty{4}
Let $p$ and $b$ be Boolean words. One step of the one-tape counter decrement machine
from its borrow state, at cell $|p|$ of the buffer tape holding $p$ followed by $b$,
behaves as follows: on an empty $b$ it enters the rewind state with failure flag one
cell to the left without writing; on a leading $\mathrm{true}$ bit it writes
$\mathrm{false}$, moves left, and enters the rewind state with success flag; on a
leading $\mathrm{false}$ bit it writes $\mathrm{true}$, moves right, and stays in the
borrow state.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[The borrow phase in exact time]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.loopBorrow_run}

\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM.loopBorrowPos, Turing.FinTM.loopBorrow_step, Turing.FinTM.loopDebit, Turing.FinTM.loopDebitCfg, Turing.FinTM.loopDebitTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step}
\difficulty{4}
Let $p$ and $u$ be Boolean words and let $j$ be the length of the maximal
$\mathrm{false}$ prefix of $u$. Starting the one-tape counter decrement machine in its
borrow state at cell $|p|$ of the buffer tape holding $p$ followed by $u$, after exactly
$j + 1$ steps it is in the rewind state carrying the decrement's success flag, at cell

\begin{lemma}[The rewind phase in exact time]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.loopBorrow_rewind}
\label{Turing.FinTM.loopBorrow_rewind}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_left, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_nat, Turing.FinTM.loopDebitCfg, Turing.FinTM.loopDebitTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_zero, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.moveInputPos_zero}
\difficulty{4}
Let $u$ be a Boolean word, $b$ a flag bit, and $j \le |u|$. Starting the one-tape
counter decrement machine in its rewind state with flag $b$ at cell $j - 1$ over the
buffer tape of $u$, after exactly $j + 1$ steps it is in the return state indexed by

\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Complete decrement-and-rewind contract]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.loopBorrow_correct}
\label{Turing.FinTM.loopBorrow_correct}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM.loopBorrowPos, Turing.FinTM.loopBorrowPos_le, Turing.FinTM.loopBorrow_rewind, Turing.FinTM.loopBorrow_run, Turing.FinTM.loopDebit, Turing.FinTM.loopDebitCfg, Turing.FinTM.loopDebitTM, Turing.FinTM.loopDebit_length, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add}
\difficulty{4}
Let $u$ be a Boolean word and $j$ the length of its maximal $\mathrm{false}$ prefix.
Then $2j + 2 \le 2|u| + 2$, and running the one-tape counter decrement machine for
exactly $2j + 2$ steps from its borrow state at cell zero over the buffer tape of $u$
ends in the return state indexed by the decrement's success flag, at cell zero, holding
the decremented word, with nothing emitted.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Stop wrapper for a loop body]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.loopBodyTM}
\label{Turing.FinTM.loopBodyTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM}
Given a bundled finite machine (the loop body) and a distinguished anchor control state,
the wrapper machine with one extra one-cell flag tape that executes the body but halts
silently at the next entry into the anchor, recording on the flag tape whether the stop
was an anchor return ($\mathrm{false}$) or a genuine body halt ($\mathrm{true}$). A set
release bit forces one body action even at the anchor, and every successor action clears
it; the body's output is retained in full.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Embedding a body configuration into the stop wrapper]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.loopBodyCfg}
\label{Turing.FinTM.loopBodyCfg}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.loopBodyTM}
For a configuration $c$ of the loop body, a release bit, and an optional flag bit, the
configuration of the stop wrapper whose body tapes carry the data of $c$, whose extra
flag tape stores the flag bit in its origin cell with head at the origin, and whose
control state is the control state of $c$ paired with the release bit.
\end{definition}

\lean{Turing.FinTM.loopBody_stop}
\label{Turing.FinTM.loopBody_stop}
\leanok

\difficulty{4}
Let $B$ be a Boolean finite Turing machine, let $a$ be one of its states, and fix an
input word $x$. If $c$ is a configuration of $B$ on $x$ in state $a$, then one step of
the stop wrapper from the embedding of $c$ with release bit false and any optional flag
$g$ equals the embedding of the same configuration with its state removed, release bit

\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[One Step of the Stop Wrapper]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.loopBody_step}
\label{Turing.FinTM.loopBody_step}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.loopBodyCfg, Turing.FinTM.loopBodyTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step}
\difficulty{5}
Let $B$ be a Boolean finite Turing machine, let $a$ be one of its states, and fix an
input word $x$. If $c$ is a configuration of $B$ on $x$ with state $q$, $r$ is a release
bit, $g$ is an optional flag bit, and it is not the case that $q=a$ and $r$ is false,
then one step of the stop wrapper from the embedding of $c$ with release bit $r$ and

\begin{lemma}[Exact Simulation Before Stopping]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.loopBody_run}
\label{Turing.FinTM.loopBody_run}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.loopBodyCfg, Turing.FinTM.loopBodyTM, Turing.FinTM.loopBody_step, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step'}
\difficulty{4}
Let $B$ be a Boolean finite Turing machine, let $a$ be one of its states, and fix an
input word $x$. Let $c$ be a configuration of $B$ on $x$ whose state is present, let $r$
be a release bit, and let $t\in\mathbb{N}$. Suppose that the configuration reached by
running $B$ from $c$ is live at every time $u<t$, and that at each such time either
$u=0$ and $r$ is true, or the state is not $a$. Then the stop wrapper, started from the
embedding of $c$ with release bit $r$ and an empty flag cell, reaches at time $t$ the
embedding of the body configuration at time $t$, with release bit $r$ if $t=0$ and false
otherwise, and with flag true exactly when that body configuration is halted (the flag
is empty when it is live).
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Capture of the stopped body in an agreeing host]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.loopBody_capture}
\label{Turing.FinTM.loopBody_capture}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.Halted, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.loopBodyCfg, Turing.FinTM.loopBodyTM, Turing.FinTM.loopBody_run, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.captureAction, Turing.captureCfg, Turing.capture_run}
\difficulty{4}
Let a host machine agree, on a family of embedded control states, with the capture
transformation of the stop wrapper of a loop body, and let $c$ be a live body
configuration together with a release bit and a time $t$ satisfying the liveness and no-
early-anchor guards. Then the host run for $t$ steps from the capture embedding of $c$
equals the capture embedding of the simulated stop-wrapper endpoint at time $t$,
including any output bit emitted by a halting transition.
\end{lemma}

\lean{Turing.FinTM.LoopHostState}
\label{Turing.FinTM.LoopHostState}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM}
The finite control type of the loop host is a disjoint sum of the fuel machine's states,
the body-call states (a stopped-body state paired with a startup marker), and fourteen
controller phases.
\end{definition}

Given a loop body and a fuel machine $F$, the multi-tape machine with the combined tape

For an input-head direction, an optional flag write, counter and payload write-and-move
pairs, an optional emitted bit, and a successor control state, the action of the loop
host that performs exactly these operations; it touches only the flag, counter, and
capture (payload) tapes, and every body and fuel tape is stationary under it.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[The concrete loop controller]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.loopHost}
\label{Turing.FinTM.loopHost}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.LoopHostState, Turing.FinTM.loopBodySource, Turing.FinTM.loopControlAction, Turing.FinTM.loopFuelSource, Turing.captureAction}
Given a loop body with anchor, a fuel machine, and an output mode, the bundled finite
machine that runs the fuel machine under capture, rewinds and copies the captured fuel
word into a fixed-width binary counter, rewinds the native input, and then repeatedly
calls the body between anchor visits: a startup call releases the first round free of
charge, each rejecting round decrements the counter in place, and the run ends either at
an accepting round -- emitting the verdict bit $\mathrm{true}$ in decision mode or
replaying the captured payload in find mode -- or at counter underflow, emitting
$\mathrm{false}$ in decision mode and nothing in find mode. Its fourteen controller
phases cover fuel rewind, counter copy, head rewinds, startup and round returns, borrow,
success and underflow rewinds, exhaustion, and payload replay.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Body calls agree with the capture discipline]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.loopHost_body_capture}
\label{Turing.FinTM.loopHost_body_capture}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.Halted, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.loopBodySource, Turing.FinTM.loopHost, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.captureCfg, Turing.capture_run}
\difficulty{1}
Let $c$ be a configuration of the extended stopped-body source on the loop host's tape
layout and $t$ a time before which that source does not halt. Then the loop host run for
$t$ steps from the capture embedding of $c$ (with the return phase determined by whether
the call is a startup call) equals the capture embedding of the source run at time $t$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Fuel Phase Captures the Fuel Run]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.loopHost_fuel_capture}
\label{Turing.FinTM.loopHost_fuel_capture}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.Halted, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.loopFuelSource, Turing.FinTM.loopHostM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.captureCfg, Turing.capture_run}
\difficulty{1}
Let $B,F$ be Boolean finite Turing machines, let $a$ be a state of $B$, choose Boolean
parameters `forward` and `findMode`, an input word $x$, a configuration $c$ of the
relocated fuel machine, and a time $t\in\mathbb N$. Suppose the relocated fuel machine
is not halted at any time $u<t$ when run from $c$. Then, after $t$ steps of the loop
host from the capture embedding of $c$ (with fuel states embedded into the host states,
controller phase $0$, and empty capture prefix and output), the resulting configuration
is exactly the capture embedding of the relocated fuel-machine configuration reached
from $c$ after $t$ steps.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Initial loop host configuration]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.loopHost_init}

\leanok

\difficulty{2}
Let $B$ and $F$ be Boolean finite Turing machines, let $a$ be a state of $B$, choose the
forward and find-mode settings, and let $x$ be a Boolean input word. The loop host's
initial configuration on $x$ equals the capture configuration of the relocated fuel
machine's initial configuration, with the fuel state embedded into the host control
states and empty capture buffers.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Idle Controller Actions]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.loopControl_idle}
\label{Turing.FinTM.loopControl_idle}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.LoopHostState, Turing.FinTM.controlAction, Turing.FinTM.loopControlAction}

For Boolean finite Turing machines $B$ and $F$, every input-head direction and every
optional loop-host successor state determine a controller action with no flag, counter,
or payload write or movement and no output. This action equals the input-only action
with that direction and successor state, which leaves every work tape and work head
unchanged.
\end{lemma}

number $t$ with $t\le c$'s input-head position plus $2$ such that after $t$ steps the
host has the same configuration data as $c$, except that its control is the startup

tape functions for the flag, counter, and payload tracks, two head positions, and an
output word, the configuration whose three active controller tracks are given by these
data and whose remaining tapes and heads are those of the base configuration.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Optional single-cell tape write]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.loopWrite}
\label{Turing.FinTM.loopWrite}
\leanok
For a tape, a head position, and an optional write instruction, the updated tape: with
no instruction the tape is unchanged, and with a write instruction exactly the cell
under the head is replaced by the written symbol.
\end{definition}

counter and payload write-and-move instructions, optional emitted bit, and successor
control state, applying the corresponding controller action to this frame gives the
frame with the successor state, the input position moved by the clamped direction, the
flag updated at the origin, and the counter and payload tapes updated at their
respective heads. The counter and payload heads move as instructed, and the emitted bit
is appended to the output; all other tapes and heads remain those of the base

\end{lemma}

A bundled finite machine over the Boolean alphabet with one work tape and a single
control state that, while its work cell holds a bit, emits that bit to the physical
output and moves right, and halts silently upon reading the right blank.

\lean{Turing.FinTM.loopHost_prepare}

on input $x$, a Boolean $e$, and a positive integer $t$. From the configuration of $B$

\difficulty{6}
Let $B$ and $F$ be Boolean finite Turing machines, let $a$ be a state of $B$, let $I$ be
a predicate on pairs of Boolean words, and let $g$, $A$, and $O$ be functions assigning
respectively a next word, an acceptance bit, and an output word to each pair of Boolean
words. Choose a Boolean mode `findMode`, an initial-word function $s_0$, and functions
$R,T:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$. Assume that $F$ computes the binary digits of $R(|x|)$ on
every input $x$ within time $T(|x|)$; that $I(x,s_0(x))$ holds and $I(x,s)$ implies
$I(x,g(x,s))$; and that for each $x$ there is a time $t\le T(|x|)$ at which $B$, started
on $x$ in its initial configuration, first reaches the seam configuration in state $a$
with tape contents given by $s_0(x)$ (it is not in state $a$ at any earlier time).
Assume also that for every $x,s$ with $I(x,s)$ there is a time $t$ with $0<t\le T(|x|)$
such that, strictly between times $0$ and $t$, the run of $B$ from the seam
configuration $(a,s)$ does not revisit state $a$; at time $t$, if $A(x,s)$ holds, the
machine is halted with output $O(x,s)$, and otherwise it is at the seam configuration
$(a,g(x,s))$. Then there is a constant $c$ such that for every input $x$ there are a
family of loop-host configurations $C_i$ and a startup time $u$ with $u\le c(T(|x|)+1)$,
the host reaches $C_0$ from its initial configuration in exactly $u$ steps, and $C_i$
has empty output for every $i\le R(|x|)$. The configuration $C_{R(|x|)+1}$ is halted,
with empty output in find mode and output $[\mathrm{false}]$ otherwise. For every $i\le
R(|x|)$ there is a time $t\le c(T(|x|)+1)$ such that, if $A(x,g^{[i]}(x,s_0(x)))$ holds,
running the host for $t$ steps from $C_i$ halts with output $O(x,g^{[i]}(x,s_0(x)))$ in
find mode and $[\mathrm{true}]$ otherwise; if it does not hold, that run reaches exactly
$C_{i+1}$. Here $g^{[i]}(x,s_0(x))$ denotes $i$ iterations of the update $s\mapsto
g(x,s)$ starting at $s_0(x)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Configuration-level loop machine]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.exists_loopCfgTM}
\label{Turing.FinTM.exists_loopCfgTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.ofWords, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesFunInTime, Turing.FinTM.loopHostTM, Turing.FinTM.loopHost_contracts, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.stateWord}
\difficulty{2}
Let $B$ and $F$ be finite Turing machines over Boolean words, let $q$ be a state of $B$,
let $I$ be a predicate on pairs of Boolean words, let $u$ map pairs of Boolean words to
Boolean words, let $A$ map such pairs to Boolean values, let $s_0$ map Boolean words to
Boolean words, and let $R,T : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$. Suppose $F$ computes the
binary digits of $R(|x|)$ within $T(|x|)$ steps; $I(x,s_0(x))$ holds and is preserved
when $s$ is replaced by $u(x,s)$; and the computation of $B$ on each input $x$ reaches
the clean seam with word $s_0(x)$ within $T(|x|)$ steps without visiting $q$ earlier.
For every $x,s$ satisfying $I(x,s)$, suppose a round from the clean seam with word $s$
takes positive time at most $T(|x|)$ and has no intermediate positive-time visit to $q$;
if $A(x,s)$ is true, it halts with output $[\mathrm{true}]$, and otherwise it reaches
the clean seam with word $u(x,s)$. Then there are a finite Turing machine $E$ and a
natural number $c$ such that, for every input $x$, there is a sequence of configurations
$(C_i)_{i\ge0}$ and a startup time at most $c(T(|x|)+1)$ reaching $C_0$, with empty
output in $C_0,\ldots,C_{R(|x|)}$, and with $C_{R(|x|)+1}$ halted and having output
$[\mathrm{false}]$. For each $i\le R(|x|)$, within at most $c(T(|x|)+1)$ steps from
$C_i$, the machine halts with output $[\mathrm{true}]$ if $A(x,u^i(s_0(x)))$ holds, and
otherwise reaches $C_{i+1}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Bounded computation of a Boolean disjunction]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.loop_halted_run}
\label{Turing.FinTM.loop_halted_run}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add}
\difficulty{5}
Let $M$ be a multi-tape Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $c_j$ be a
configuration on a common input for each $0\le j\le N$, and let $a$ be a Boolean-valued
function on the natural numbers. Suppose $c_N$ is halted with output the one-bit word
$[\mathrm{false}]$. For every $j<N$, assume there is a time $t\le B$ such that, if
$a(j)$ is true, the run from $c_j$ is halted at time $t$ with output $[\mathrm{true}]$;
if $a(j)$ is false, the run from $c_j$ at time $t$ equals $c_{j+1}$. Then there is a
time $t\le NB$ at which the run from $c_0$ is halted and has output the one-bit word
whose value is true exactly when $a(j)$ is true for some $j<N$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Decision loop machine]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.exists_loopTM}
\label{Turing.FinTM.exists_loopTM}
\leanok

\difficulty{4}
Let $B$ and $F$ be finite Turing machines over Boolean words, let $q$ be a state of $B$,
let $I$ be a predicate on pairs of Boolean words, let $u$ map such pairs to Boolean
words, let $A$ be Boolean-valued on such pairs, let $s_0$ map Boolean words to Boolean
words, and let $R,T : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$. Suppose $F$ computes the binary
digits of $R(|x|)$ within $T(|x|)$ steps, $I(x,s_0(x))$ holds, and $I(x,s)$ implies
$I(x,u(x,s))$. Suppose startup on each input $x$ reaches the clean seam with word
$s_0(x)$ within $T(|x|)$ steps without visiting $q$ earlier. For every $x,s$ satisfying
$I(x,s)$, suppose a round takes positive time at most $T(|x|)$ with no intermediate
positive-time visit to $q$; it halts with output $[\mathrm{true}]$ if $A(x,s)$ holds,
and otherwise reaches the clean seam with word $u(x,s)$. Then there are a finite Turing
machine $E$ and a natural number $c$ such that $E$ computes the one-bit word indicating
whether $A(x,u^i(x,s_0(x)))$ holds for some $i\le R(|x|)$, within $c(T(n)+1)(R(n)+2)$
steps on inputs of length $n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[First accepting payload within a step bound]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.loop_find_run}
\label{Turing.FinTM.loop_find_run}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add}
\difficulty{5}
Let $M$ be a multi-tape Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet with state set $S$, let
$x$ be a Boolean input word, and let $c$ assign a configuration of $M$ on $x$ to each
natural number. Let $a$ assign a Boolean acceptance flag and $y$ a Boolean payload word
to each natural number, and let $B,N$ be natural numbers. Suppose $c(N)$ is halted with
empty output. Suppose also that for every $j<N$ there is a time $t\le B$ such that, if
$a(j)$ is true, the run from $c(j)$ is halted at time $t$ with output $y(j)$; if $a(j)$
is false, the run from $c(j)$ at time $t$ is exactly $c(j+1)$. Then from $c(0)$ the
machine halts within $N B$ steps with output $y(i)$ for the first index $i<N$ with
$a(i)$ true, if such an index exists, and with empty output if none exists.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Result-bearing loop machine]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.exists_loopFindTM}
\label{Turing.FinTM.exists_loopFindTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg.ofWords, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesFunInTime, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime.mono, Turing.FinTM.loopHostTM, Turing.FinTM.loopHost_contracts, Turing.FinTM.loop_find_run, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, Turing.stateWord}
\difficulty{4}
Let $B$ and $F$ be finite Turing machines over Boolean words, let $q$ be a state of $B$,
let $I$ be a predicate on pairs of Boolean words, let $u,A,o$ be functions on pairs of
Boolean words, where $A$ is Boolean-valued and $o$ is word-valued, and let $s_0$ map
Boolean words to Boolean words. Let $R,T : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$. Suppose $F$
computes the binary digits of $R(|x|)$ within $T(|x|)$ steps, $I(x,s_0(x))$ holds, and
$I(x,s)$ implies $I(x,u(x,s))$. Suppose startup on each $x$ reaches the clean seam with
word $s_0(x)$ within $T(|x|)$ steps without visiting $q$ earlier. For every $x,s$ with
$I(x,s)$, suppose a round takes positive time at most $T(|x|)$ without an intermediate
positive-time visit to $q$; if $A(x,s)$ holds, it halts with output $o(x,s)$, and
otherwise it reaches the clean seam with word $u(x,s)$. Then there are a finite Turing
machine $E$ and a natural number $c$ such that $E$ computes within $c(T(n)+1)(R(n)+2)$
steps the word $o(x,u^i(x,s_0(x)))$ for the least $i\le R(|x|)$ with
$A(x,u^i(x,s_0(x)))$, if such an index exists, and the empty word if none exists.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Capture-wrapped candidate evaluator]

virtual-input simulator of $M$ (reading its argument from a designated work tape rather
than the native input) with the capture transformation: every emission of the simulated

evaluator in which the preserved argument occupies tape zero, the simulated work bank of

head is fixed at the given position.

$c$, $b$, and $p$ gives exactly the evaluator configuration associated with the time-$t$
configuration of $M$, tag $b'$, and the same physical position $p$.

\begin{definition}[Three-tape interval cleaner]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.emCallClearTM}
\label{Turing.FinTM.emCallClearTM}

\uses{Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.controlAction}
A bundled finite machine over the Boolean alphabet with three work tapes -- data, an
interval marker, and an origin marker -- and four control states, that scans left to the
marked interval's left end, erases the data and the marker in one rightward pass,
rewinds on the surviving origin marker, and finishes in a silent absorbing return state
with all three heads at the origin. All three heads move together, and only observed
tape symbols dispatch control.
\end{definition}

for data, interval marks, and the origin marker, and a common head position $h$, the
configuration of the three-tape interval cleaner whose tapes are as given, whose three
work heads are all at $h$, and whose output is empty.
\end{definition}

configuration equals the completed tracked configuration of $c$, with each span extended

\begin{lemma}[The interval cleaner's time bound]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.emCall_track_clearable}
\label{Turing.FinTM.emCall_track_clearable}

\uses{Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.FinTM.emCallClearCfg, Turing.FinTM.emCallClearTM, Turing.FinTM.emCallHi, Turing.FinTM.emCallLo, Turing.FinTM.emCallSpan, Turing.FinTM.emCall_clear_run, Turing.FinTM.emCall_span_interval, Turing.FinTM.emCall_track_extent, Turing.FinTM.emCall_track_support, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom}
\difficulty{5}
Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over Booleans, let $x,w$ be Boolean words, let $p$ be
one of the $|w|+2$ input-head positions, let $T\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $i$ be a
work-tape index of $M$. There is an integer time $t$ with $0<t\le 6T+7$ such that the
three-tape cleaner, started on input $w$ at position $p$ in state $0$, has as its data
tape the contents of tape $i$ of $M$ after $T$ steps on $x$, as its marker tape the
closed span from the leftmost to the rightmost head position visited by tape $i$ through
time $T$, and as its origin tape the marker at zero, with all three heads at tape $i$'s
time-$T$ head position, reaches state $3$ with all three tapes blank and all three heads
at the origin. Its output is empty.
\end{lemma}

from a configuration $c$ reaches a configuration $d$ in a stop state at time $T$, then
there is a time $t\le T$ at which the run equals $d$ and no stop state has been visited
at any earlier time $j<t$.
\end{lemma}

words, let $p$ be an input-head position for $w$, let $T$ be a nonnegative integer, and
let $i$ be a work-tape index of $M$. Write $d$ for the content of tape $i$ after $M$
runs on $x$ for $T$ steps, write $\ell$ and $h$ for the least and greatest head
positions of that tape up to time $T$, and let the interval marker be true on $[\ell,h]$
and blank elsewhere; place a single origin marker at cell $0$, and start the three-tape
cleaner with all heads at the head position of tape $i$ at time $T$. There is a time $t$
with $0<t\le 6T+7$ such that the cleaner is not in state $3$ at any time $j<t$, and at
time $t$ it is in state $3$ with all three tapes blank and all heads at the origin.

\begin{definition}[Two-tape result finalizer]

the captured result) and six control states that, entering at the known right blanks of
both words, rewinds the argument -- erasing it in install mode, preserving it in emit

erases the capture and returns both heads to the origin, finishing in an absorbing
silent state.

start the two-tape finalizer in state $1$, with its argument tape storing $\mathrm{arg}$
when $\mathrm{emit}$ is true and $\mathrm{pre}$ otherwise, its argument head at
$|\mathrm{pre}|-1$, its capture tape storing $\mathrm{cap}$ with its head at
$|\mathrm{cap}|$, and empty output. After exactly $|\mathrm{pre}|+1$ steps it is in
state $2$, with the argument tape storing $\mathrm{arg}$ when $\mathrm{emit}$ is true
and the empty word otherwise, the argument head at the origin, the capture tape still
storing $\mathrm{cap}$ with its head at $|\mathrm{cap}|-1$, and empty output.

is in state $3$, with the capture tape unchanged and its head at the origin, argument
head still at the origin, and output empty.

its head at $|c|-1$, the argument head at $|c|-1$ in install mode and at $0$ in emit

\begin{definition}[The native clean-call controller]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.emCallTM}
\label{Turing.FinTM.emCallTM}
\leanok

For a bundled finite machine $M$ and a mode bit, the controller machine that evaluates
$M$ on a tape-resident argument through the prepared tracked source and captures the
result at its observed return, then sequentially runs the interval cleaner on each

result on the argument tape (install mode) or forwards it to the physical output while
preserving the argument (emit mode), erasing the capture. No deadline or source running
time occurs in its transition table.

\begin{definition}[Loop body dispatch action]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.loopBodyDispatch}
\label{Turing.FinTM.loopBodyDispatch}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.LoopHostState, Turing.FinTM.leftAction, Turing.FinTM.loopBodySource, Turing.captureAction, Turing.emitAction}
Let $body$ and $F$ be finite Boolean-alphabet Turing machines, let $anchor$ be a state
of $body$, and let $forward$, $startup$, and the second component of the body-call state
be Boolean data. Given the current input symbol and the work-tape symbols for the
combined machine, the loop body dispatch produces an action of that machine: in forward
mode it routes the body machine's transition through the left-action and output-emission
construction, and otherwise it routes that transition through the capture construction.
In either case it maps the body state into the loop host's body-call states, recording
the startup marker and selecting controller phase $6$ for startup or phase $7$
otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Loop host machine construction]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.loopHostM}
\label{Turing.FinTM.loopHostM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.LoopHostState, Turing.FinTM.loopBodyDispatch, Turing.FinTM.loopControlAction, Turing.FinTM.loopFuelSource, Turing.captureAction}
Given finite Turing machines $B$ and $F$ over the Boolean alphabet, a state $a$ of $B$,
and Boolean parameters $f$ and $m$, one can construct a finite Boolean-alphabet Turing
machine with $B.k+1+(1+F.k)+1$ work tapes. Its states comprise states of $F$, body-call
states carrying a startup bit, a state of $B$, and a Boolean marker, and fourteen
controller states; its initial state is the initial state of $F$. Its transitions
combine transitions of $F$ and $B$ with controller actions that manage calls, tape
regions, a counter, and a payload, with terminal behavior determined by the parameters
$f$ and $m$.
\end{definition}

\lean{Turing.FinTM.loopHostTM}

\leanok

For finite machines $body$ and $F$ over the Boolean alphabet, a state $anchor$ of
$body$, and a Boolean find-mode flag, the loop host machine is the loop host
construction with its forward flag set to false.
\end{definition}

Let $B$ and $F$ be Boolean finite Turing machines, let $a$ be a state of $B$, and let

each input, and let $R,T:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. Assume $F$ computes the word of
binary digits of $R(|x|)$ on each input $x$ in time $T(|x|)$; $I(x,s_0(x))$ holds for
every $x$ and is preserved by $g$; and for each $x$, the run of $B$ from its initial
configuration reaches the seam configuration at state $a$ with tape words assigned by
$s_0(x)$ within some time $t\le T(|x|)$, without having state $a$ at any earlier time.
Also assume that for every $x,s$ with $I(x,s)$, there is a time $t$ with $0<t\le T(|x|)$
such that the run of $B$ from the seam configuration at $a$ with tape words assigned by
$s$ does not have state $a$ at any intermediate time $t'$ with $0<t'<t$; at time $t$, if
$A(x,s)$ is true the run is halted with output $O(x,s)$, and otherwise it is the seam
configuration at $a$ with tape words assigned by $g(x,s)$. Then for every input $x$
there are a sequence of loop-host configurations $c_i$ and a startup time $u$ such that
$u\le 10(T(|x|)+1)$, the loop host's run from its initial configuration at time $u$ is
$c_0$, every $c_i$ for $i\le R(|x|)$ has empty output, and $c_{R(|x|)+1}$ is halted with
output $[]$ in find mode and $[\mathrm{false}]$ otherwise. Moreover, for every $i\le
R(|x|)$ there is a time $t\le 10(T(|x|)+1)$ such that, if $A(x,g^{[i]}(s_0(x)))$ is
true, the run from $c_i$ is halted at time $t$ with output $[]$ in find mode and
$[\mathrm{true}]$ otherwise; if it is false, that run at time $t$ equals $c_{i+1}$. Here
$g^{[i]}$ denotes $i$-fold iteration of $s\mapsto g(x,s)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Loop host decides bounded acceptance]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.loopHostTM_decides}
\label{Turing.FinTM.loopHostTM_decides}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg.ofWords, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesFunInTime, Turing.FinTM.loopHostTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.stateWord}
Let $B$ and $F$ be Boolean finite Turing machines, let $a$ be a state of $B$, let $I$ be
a predicate on pairs of Boolean words, $g$ a state-update function, $A$ a Boolean
acceptance test, and $s_0$ an initial-word function. Let $R,T:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$.
Assume $F$ computes the binary digits of $R(|x|)$ on each input $x$ within time
$T(|x|)$; $I(x,s_0(x))$ holds for every $x$ and is preserved by $g$; and for each $x$,
the run of $B$ from its initial configuration reaches the seam configuration at state
$a$ with tape words assigned by $s_0(x)$ within some time $t\le T(|x|)$, without having
state $a$ at any earlier time. Also assume that for every $x,s$ with $I(x,s)$, there is
a time $t$ with $0<t\le T(|x|)$ such that the run of $B$ from the seam configuration at
$a$ with tape words assigned by $s$ has no state-$a$ visit at any time $t'$ with
$0<t'<t$; at time $t$, if $A(x,s)$ is true the run is halted with output
$[\mathrm{true}]$, and otherwise it is the seam configuration at $a$ with tape words
assigned by $g(x,s)$. Then the loop host in decision mode computes, on every Boolean
input $x$, the one-bit word whose bit is true exactly when $A(x,g^{[i]}(s_0(x)))$ holds
for some $0\le i\le R(|x|)$, in time $10(T(|x|)+1)(R(|x|)+2)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Loop host finds the first accepted state]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.loopHostTM_finds}
\label{Turing.FinTM.loopHostTM_finds}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg.ofWords, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesFunInTime, Turing.FinTM.loopHostTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.stateWord}
Let $B$ and $F$ be Boolean finite Turing machines, let $a$ be a state of $B$, let $I$ be
a predicate on pairs of Boolean words, $g$ a state-update function, $A$ a Boolean
acceptance test, $O$ an output-word function, and $s_0$ an initial-word function. Let
$R,T:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. Assume $F$ computes the binary digits of $R(|x|)$ on each
input $x$ within time $T(|x|)$; $I(x,s_0(x))$ holds for every $x$ and is preserved by
$g$; and for each $x$, the run of $B$ from its initial configuration reaches the seam
configuration at state $a$ with tape words assigned by $s_0(x)$ within some time $t\le
T(|x|)$, without having state $a$ at any earlier time. Also assume that for every $x,s$
with $I(x,s)$, there is a time $t$ with $0<t\le T(|x|)$ such that the run of $B$ from
the seam configuration at $a$ with tape words assigned by $s$ has no state-$a$ visit at
any time $t'$ with $0<t'<t$; at time $t$, if $A(x,s)$ is true the run is halted with
output $O(x,s)$, and otherwise it is the seam configuration at $a$ with tape words
assigned by $g(x,s)$. Then the loop host in find mode computes, on every Boolean input
$x$, the output $O(x,g^{[i]}(s_0(x)))$ for the least $i$ in $0,\ldots,R(|x|)$ with
$A(x,g^{[i]}(s_0(x)))$ true, and computes the empty word if no such $i$ exists, in time
$10(T(|x|)+1)(R(|x|)+2)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Loop host space bound]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.loopHostTM_spaceUsed_le_budget}
\label{Turing.FinTM.loopHostTM_spaceUsed_le_budget}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg.ofWords, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesFunInTime, Turing.FinTM.loopHostTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.spaceUsed, Turing.stateWord}
Let $B$ and $F$ be finite Boolean Turing machines, let $a$ be a state of $B$, let
$I(x,s)$ be a predicate on Boolean words, and let $g(x,s)$ and $A(x,s)$ be
Boolean-word-valued functions, with $A(x,s)$ Boolean-valued. Let $s_0$ assign a Boolean
word to each Boolean word, and let $R,T:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$. Suppose that on every
input $x$, $F$ halts within $T(|x|)$ steps with output the binary expansion of $R(|x|)$;
that $I(x,s_0(x))$ holds for every $x$; and that $I(x,s)$ implies $I(x,g(x,s))$. Suppose
also that, for every $x$, the run of $B$ from its initial configuration on $x$ reaches
the anchor state $a$ in some $t\le T(|x|)$, has not visited $a$ at any earlier time, and
at time $t$ is exactly the anchor configuration with $s_0(x)$ on tape zero and all other
work tapes blank. Finally, suppose that for every $x,s$ with $I(x,s)$ there is a
positive time $t\le T(|x|)$ such that the run of $B$ from that anchor configuration has
no intermediate anchor visit; if $A(x,s)$ holds, it halts at time $t$ with output
$g(x,s)$, and otherwise it is at the anchor configuration with $g(x,s)$ on tape zero and
all other work tapes blank. Then, for every input $x$ and time $t$, the loop host with
body $B$, fuel machine $F$, anchor $a$, and the specified mode uses at most
$23K(T(|x|)+1)$ work-tape cells through time $t$, where $K$ is its number of work tapes.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Embedded call configuration]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.emCallEmbeddedCfg}
\label{Turing.FinTM.emCallEmbeddedCfg}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.mapState, Turing.embedEmitCfg}
Let $x$ be a finite Boolean input, let $S$ and $H$ be state types, and let $k$ and $l$
be natural numbers. Given an injection from the $k$ work-tape indices into the $l$
indices, a map from $S$ to $H$, tape contents and head positions for the $l$ tapes, and
a configuration on $x$ with $k$ work tapes and states in $S$, the embedded call
configuration is the configuration with $l$ work tapes and states in $H$ obtained by
embedding the emitting configuration using the given tape data and mapping its state by
the given map.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Embedding of a tracked tape triple]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.emCallTripleEmbedding}
\label{Turing.FinTM.emCallTripleEmbedding}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.emCallSource, Turing.FinTM.emCallTripleIndex, Turing.FinTM.emCallTripleSelect, Turing.FinTM.emCall_triple_inverse}
For a finite Boolean Turing machine $M$ and one of its work tapes $i$, the embedding of
the three roles—data, visited mark, and origin mark—into the work tapes of the prepared
source machine sends those roles to their corresponding slots in the three consecutive
tape banks.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Embedding of the argument and capture tapes]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.emCallPairEmbedding}
\label{Turing.FinTM.emCallPairEmbedding}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.emCallPairIndex, Turing.FinTM.emCallPairSelect, Turing.FinTM.emCallSource, Turing.FinTM.emCall_pair_inverse}
For a finite Boolean Turing machine $M$, the embedding of the two roles used by the
finalizer into the prepared source machine's work tapes sends the argument role to the
first tape and the capture role to the last tape.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Clean-call machine]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.callTM}
\label{Turing.FinTM.callTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action.mapState, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.controlAction, Turing.FinTM.emCallClearTM, Turing.FinTM.emCallFinishTM, Turing.FinTM.emCallPairEmbedding, Turing.FinTM.emCallRightTM, Turing.FinTM.emCallSource, Turing.FinTM.emCallState, Turing.FinTM.emCallTrackTM, Turing.FinTM.emCallTripleEmbedding, Turing.embedEmitTM}
Given a finite Boolean Turing machine $M$ and a Boolean flag $e$, the clean-call machine
has the prepared source machine's work tapes and a control state that combines its
source states with states for clearing each source tape and for finalizing the result.
It begins by simulating the prepared source phase; it then runs the interval cleaner on
the source tapes in turn, and finally runs the two-tape result finalizer, whose behavior
is selected by $e$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Initial state of the clean-call machine]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.callEntry}
\label{Turing.FinTM.callEntry}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.callTM}
For a finite Boolean Turing machine $M$ and a Boolean flag $e$, the entry state of the
clean-call machine is its initial state: the prepared source phase's initial state, with
its input-boundary tag set to true.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Final state of the clean-call machine]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.callExit}
\label{Turing.FinTM.callExit}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.callTM}
For a finite Boolean Turing machine $M$ and a Boolean flag $e$, the exit state of the
clean-call machine is the finalizer's state numbered five.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Positive work-tape count for the call machine]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.callTM_k_pos}
\label{Turing.FinTM.callTM_k_pos}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.callTM}
\difficulty{1}
For every finite-state machine $M$ over the Boolean alphabet and every Boolean parameter
$e$, the call machine formed from $M$ with parameter $e$ has a strictly positive number
of work tapes.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Emit-mode loop machine]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.emitLoopTM}
\label{Turing.FinTM.emitLoopTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.emLoopHost}
Given finite Boolean Turing machines $B$ and $F$ and a state $a$ of $B$, the emit-loop
machine is the loop-host construction applied to $B$, $F$, and $a$ in emit mode.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Correctness and running time of the emitting loop]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.emitLoopTM_computes}
\label{Turing.FinTM.emitLoopTM_computes}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg.ofWords, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesFunInTime, Turing.FinTM.emitLoopTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.stateWord}
Let $B$ and $F$ be Boolean finite Turing machines and let $a$ be a state of $B$. Let $I$
be a relation on pairs of Boolean words, let $g,h$ be functions on pairs of Boolean
words, and let $s_0$ and $R,T$ be functions as follows: $g(x,s)$ is the next round word,
$h(x,s)$ is the output of a round, and $s_0(x)$ is the initial round word. Suppose $F$
computes the function $x\mapsto \operatorname{bits}(R(|x|))$ within time $T$,
$I(x,s_0(x))$ holds for every $x$, and $I(x,s)$ implies $I(x,g(x,s))$. Assume that for
each input $x$, the run of $B$ from its initial configuration reaches the seam at state
$a$ with word $s_0(x)$ within $T(|x|)$ steps, without visiting $a$ at any earlier time.
Also assume that whenever $I(x,s)$ holds, there is a positive duration at most $T(|x|)$
in which $B$, started at the seam with word $s$, avoids $a$ at all strictly intermediate
positive times and ends at the seam with word $g(x,s)$ and output $h(x,s)$. Then the
emitting loop machine computes, on every input $x$, the concatenation of the $R(|x|)+1$
round outputs $h(x,g_x^{[i]}(s_0(x)))$ for $0\le i\le R(|x|)$, within time
$10(T(|x|)+1)(R(|x|)+2)$, where $g_x(s)=g(x,s)$ and $g_x^{[i]}$ denotes $i$-fold
iteration.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Bounded clean call computation]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.callTM_run}
\label{Turing.FinTM.callTM_run}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg.ofWords, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.FinTM.callEntry, Turing.FinTM.callExit, Turing.FinTM.callTM, Turing.FinTM.emCall_first, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.stateWord}
\difficulty{1}
Let $M$ be a finite-state machine over the Boolean alphabet, let
$e\in\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$, and let $x$, $a$, and $c$ be Boolean words.
Suppose $M$ halts on input word $a$ with output word $c$ after $T$ steps. Then there is
a positive natural number $t$ with $t\le (24+13k)(T+|a|+|c|+1)$, where $k$ is the number
of work tapes of $M$, such that the call machine's run from its entry state, with $a$ on
tape zero and all other work tapes blank, does not reach its exit state at any time
$j<t$. At time $t$ its configuration is the exit-state configuration with $a$ on tape
zero and empty output if $e$ is true, and with $c$ on tape zero and output $c$ if $e$ is
false; all other work tapes are blank, the input head is at its initial position, and
the other configuration data have their initial values.
\end{theorem}
